patch.value: pm-brief consumes a truncated `pm list-all` answer as if it were complete

Every brief/delta/divergence/governance read goes through readPmItems -> pm list-all --json --include-body and takes .items without checking the answer's completeness receipt. Under pm-cli 2026.8.14 the default output budget returned 10 of 682 workspace items with truncated=true, and pm-brief rendered a full brief from that silent subset and reported success. truncated can still go true under an output budget and completeness.status can go partial when item documents are unreadable, so the read itself must refuse those answers instead of exporting half a workspace.

The CommandError names every tripped signal plus count vs total. next_cursor is deliberately NOT followed: pm-brief has no paging consumer, refusing loudly is the contract. Also exact-pinned @unbrained/pm-cli to 2026.8.15 in devDependencies and peerDependencies (the >=2026.8.7 peer floor auto-installed whatever was newest, which is how 2026.8.14 reached consumers with no diff here). Revert-proof: with the parsePmItemsOutput refusal reverted, the new regression tests fail with 'AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Missing expected exception: the refusal must name the truncated signal and the counts' - six tests fail (no-receipt, truncated, has_more, completeness.status, omission_receipt.has_omissions, malformed-rows contract), only the happy-path test still passes.

patch.value: parsePmItemsOutput refuses any pm list-all --json answer that cannot prove it is the whole workspace, naming every tripped signal and the count-versus-total split. Six independent signals are checked: truncated, has_more, a completeness.status that is not "complete" (an absent completeness block counts as incomplete), omission_receipt.has_omissions, an absent or malformed omission_receipt, and a non-null next_cursor. The last two were added in review: the receipt must be PRESENT and say no omissions rather than merely fail to say otherwise, and a continuation cursor means rows remain beyond this answer whether or not has_more agrees, which is checked independently because only has_more was being read. This package deliberately does not page, so it refuses loudly rather than running a hand-rolled resumption loop that can itself half-fail. Dependency shape: devDependencies pins @unbrained/pm-cli EXACTLY at 2026.8.15, because it decides which CLI the gates run against and must be reproducible; peerDependencies declares a LOWER-BOUND floor of >=2026.8.15, because an exact peer pin would make every later CLI patch a peer conflict for consumers under strict peer resolution.

Review round 2 (CodeRabbit on PR #69) — all three findings adopted.

ADOPTED (Major, and it exposed a doc-versus-code gap) — `collectIncompleteListAllSignals` checked four signals; two more were needed, and one of them the docstring already claimed:

1. `omission_receipt` was only refused when it explicitly said `has_omissions: true`. An ABSENT or malformed receipt passed. That contradicts the principle stated two lines above it for `completeness` — "an answer that cannot prove its own completeness must not be consumed as if it had". Verified against the real CLI: every build at this package's declared `>=2026.8.15` peer floor emits `omission_receipt: { has_omissions: false, ... }` on `list-all --full --include-body`, so a missing receipt is not an older-CLI shape to tolerate. Now refused, distinguishing `omission_receipt=<missing>` from `has_omissions=<missing>`.

2. `next_cursor` was never read at all, despite the docstring asserting that it "is deliberately NOT followed... refusing loudly beats a hand-rolled resumption loop". Only `has_more` was checked, so an envelope carrying a cursor with `has_more` absent or false was consumed as the whole workspace. Now checked independently, because they are two separate claims. Verified the real CLI emits `next_cursor: null` when the answer is whole.

ADOPTED — the closure record stated the CLI is "exact-pinned at 2026.8.15 in devDependencies and peerDependencies". Only the dev pin is exact; the peer declaration is the lower-bound range `>=2026.8.15`, which is deliberate — an exact peer pin makes every later CLI patch a peer conflict for consumers under strict peer resolution, turning a compatibility statement into a lockstep release dependency. Corrected.

ADOPTED — the closed item carried no `resolution` field; `close_reason` does not substitute for it. Both are now set through `pm update`, recorded as an append-only event with no history file edited.

Three new refusal cases added to the signal table (absent receipt, malformed receipt, absent `has_omissions`, non-null cursor), each verified non-vacuous by reverting the check. 223 tests plus the new cases pass, release:check green.
